title: Weights of finite-dimensional Frobenius modules
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, and let $q=p^a$ be the
fixed prime power. Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers],
choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and fix an isomorphism
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$. For a finite-dimensional
$\Qlb$-vector space $V$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], a $\Qlb$-linear automorphism $F:V\to V$ (thus a Frobenius module [sk-def-frobmod]), and $w\in\mathbf R$, call
$(V,F)$ $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ if every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $F$
satisfies $|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{w/2}$, where $|\cdot|$ is the complex absolute value [def-weil-complex-absolute-value]. Call $(V,F)$ $\iota$-mixed of weights at
most $w$ if there are an integer $m\geq0$, an $F$-stable filtration

$$
 0=V_0\subseteq V_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq V_m=V
$$

and real numbers $w_1,\ldots,w_m\leq w$ such that each $(V_r/V_{r-1},F)$ is
$\iota$-pure of weight $w_r$.

Here an eigenvalue of a linear operator $A$ on a vector space is a scalar
$\alpha$ for which there is a vector $v\ne0$ with $A(v)=\alpha v$.
An $F$-stable filtration means a finite increasing family of
$\Qlb$-linear subspaces $V_r\subseteq V$ with the displayed endpoints
and $F(V_r)=V_r$ for every $0\le r\le m$.
The successive quotient $V_r/V_{r-1}$ is the quotient vector space
[def-weil-pbc-quotient-module], and its induced Frobenius is
$v+V_{r-1}\mapsto F(v)+V_{r-1}$ for $v\in V_r$.
The number $q^{w/2}$ is the real power of the positive real number $q$ [def-weil-real-power].
The isomorphism $\iota$ is an isomorphism of fields, with no continuity
condition. Neither $F$ nor the operators on the successive quotients
are required to be semisimple. The case $m=0$ is allowed, when the
endpoint conditions require $V=0$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q61-793ee68d4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all of def-weil-frobenius-module-weights against both blueprint snapshots, master order 2651 and main-20261015 order 2995. The two texts are identical. All hypotheses are kept: p is prime, a>=1, q=p^a, l is a prime different from p, Qlb is an algebraic closure of Q_l, iota is a field isomorphism, w is real, and nothing requires integrality or semisimplicity. The clarifications are equivalent to the source. First, F(V_r) contained in V_r is the same as F(V_r)=V_r, because F is injective and V_r is finite-dimensional. Second, strict and non-strict inclusions give the same predicate, because a zero quotient is pure of every weight and can be deleted. Third, the induced map on V_r/V_{r-1} is a well-defined automorphism, so applying the purity predicate to the quotients is legitimate. I tested V=0 (m=0), a 1-dimensional scalar c, the non-semisimple Jordan block with eigenvalue 1 (pure of weight 0), and diag(1,q), which is mixed of weights at most 2 but not at most 1. I read all six cited statements and they say what the item takes from them (sk-def-frobmod: first sentence only, a notion rather than a route). Dropping def-weil-finite-field-fiber is accepted: the item introduces p, a, q, l and Qlb itself, so it is a parametric form with the same meaning. No duplicates: def-weil-punctual-weights and sk-d-real-weights are about sheaves, sk-def-roots is about polynomials, def-tw-eigenvalue is a q-adic normalization, and lem-a1-punctual-bound-module-mixed is a downstream user. There are no new nodes, no proof steps, no tool_uses and no SGA. Fault fixed (B3): q^{w/2} was defined inline without citing the existing node def-weil-real-power (mathlib, Real.rpow, no dependencies). I added [def-weil-real-power] to that sentence and to stmt_deps in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-purity-real-sheaves/def-weil-frobenius-module-weights.json. This adds no cycle and changes nothing else.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
